html:
An Arabic book of machines written around 850 in Baghdad by the three Banu Musa brothers, Muhammad, Ahmad and al-Hasan, the sons of Musa ibn Shakir. It describes about 100 devices.

Most are trick vessels and automatic fountains: jugs that pour two different drinks, basins that refill themselves, fountains that change shape. There is also a lamp that trims its own wick and a mechanical grab for pulling things out of water. They work with floats, valves, siphons and air pressure, and some use simple automatic control, switching on and off by themselves.

The brothers built on Greek writers such as Hero of Alexandria, whose work reached them through the translation movement. They were rich patrons of translators and also worked in astronomy and geometry at the Abbasid court. Their book began an Arabic tradition of engineering that peaked with al-Jazari's book of machines in 1206.
sum: An Arabic book of machines written around 850 in Baghdad by the three Banu Musa brothers, Muhammad, Ahmad and al-Hasan, the sons of Musa ibn Shakir. It describes about 100 devices.
